objective: Test whether a target/sink-native current-state CAS keyed by a stable applied_transition_id closes the same-provider-ID repository-witness rollback gap without external hosted coordination, richer-mode arbitration, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental monetary cost.
semantic_inputs_used: Own role-local LATEST.json and Part95 checkpoint only after the frozen control tuple and durable presemantic witness.
No other-worker, downstream, O-derived, shared-ledger, or legacy semantic input was read.
No new public semantic source was required for this bounded abstract anti-ABA model; Part95 remains the source-qualified predecessor for the repository/provider-ID premise.

model.weighting: Equal-weight finite mechanism lattice; counts are mechanism/counterexample counts, not production probabilities.

candidate_semantics.A_repository_witness_only: Repository current-blob witness plus applied_transition_id; no target-native current-state compare.
candidate_semantics.B_sink_current_state_cas: Before an authoritative effect, atomically compare the target/sink current state expected by the transition, consume stable applied_transition_id, and advance target state with the effect. A newer target state or retained transition ID rejects replay. Repository transport interruption fails closed.
candidate_semantics.C_independent_monotonic_control: Hypothetical anti-rollback monotonic floor plus durable single-use transition identity outside both repository and sink rollback domains; this is a non-accepted positive control because it assumes the missing independent authority.

model.anti_rollback_gap_definition: For B, the intentionally adversarial residual case is joint repository rewind + sink state rollback + loss of the sink's durable transition-id retention. In that state both mutable authority domains can again present the pre-effect state.

A_repository_witness_only.interpretation: Part95's rollback gap persists: a rewound repository witness can re-authorize an old same-provider transition and can also forget an applied_transition_id after an ambiguous response.

B_sink_current_state_cas.interpretation: A target-native CAS materially narrows the repository-only failure surface and removes stale/duplicate effects whenever either the target state remains ahead or its transition identity survives. It does not provide an anti-rollback proof when the target authority state and its replay memory can both be restored behind the real history.

C_hypothetical_independent_monotonic_con.reason: The positive result assumes monotonic evidence outside both rollback domains, which is the unresolved coordination capability and cannot be imported as a zero-dependency solution.

finding.new_positive_narrow_scope: In the 56 repository-available scenarios outside the joint repository-rewind + sink-rollback + transition-retention-loss gap, target/sink current-state CAS had 0 stale-authority effects and 0 duplicate authoritative effects. This is a strictly narrower capability result, not Phase-1 acceptance.
finding.new_falsification: When repository witness state and sink authoritative state are both rolled back and the sink's transition-id memory is also lost, B produced 4 stale-authority counterexamples and 2 duplicate-authoritative-effect counterexamples across eight repository-available scenarios. Four same-provider-ABA scenarios in that joint gap were all stale-authority failures.
finding.minimal_unresolved_child: A repository/target-native anti-rollback witness whose effect identity remains monotonic across restore/force-rewind of every mutable authority domain participating in the effect, or a target primitive whose append-only/irreversible effect journal cannot be restored behind an already-applied transition. The mechanism must remain zero-cost, zero-finite-quota, Chat-native, and require no richer-mode/protected/manual step or external hosted coordinator.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport_role: Lightweight state/evidence transport only; repository interruption blocks authoritative effects and is not used as compute.

scope_guard: This result is limited to the stated 128-scenario abstract model and Part95's already-source-qualified repository/provider-identity premise. It does not claim a production failure rate, does not assert undocumented sink guarantees, and does not prove that any concrete target exposes the strong CAS or anti-rollback primitive modeled here.
frontier: Target-native append-only or irreversible effect journal versus mutable CAS state under restore/rollback.
Retention/compaction boundary for stable applied_transition_id at the target.
Whether a repository-native immutable object plus current ref authority can supply useful anti-rollback evidence without leaving the repository rollback domain.
Fail-closed recovery when every available authority surface is rollback-equivalent.
continuation: Part97: execute exactly one bounded target-native append-only-effect-journal leaf. Compare mutable sink CAS state, target-local append-only transition journal with current-state precondition, and the same hypothetical independent anti-rollback floor as a non-accepted control. Cover target restore/delete-recreate, journal retention/compaction loss, repository witness rewind, ambiguous effect response, takeover/retry, same-provider ABA, and repository interruption. Accept only if a concrete repository/target-native mechanism can keep stale-authority and duplicate-authoritative effects at zero with zero residual richer-mode/protected/manual execution, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota, zero incremental cost, and no external hosted coordinator; otherwise preserve the exact target-journal anti-rollback residual child.
